profiles.meeting_scenario: A county resilience program is preparing to use a fast-updating disaster response simulation during an active severe-weather season, so the emergency management coordination team and the modeling team are meeting to align handoffs between the simulation workstream and the operational planning workstream. The context is a coordination meeting between the county Emergency Management Office and a university-affiliated simulation lab that models how cumulative flood, heat, and infrastructure disruptions increase community demand while response capacity erodes across agencies and NGOs. The agenda is to confirm which inputs the model will ingest this week, what version of the interagency network and capacity data should be treated as the baseline, when the next fragility run will be considered ready for the county planning cell, and how the update will be posted into the shared operating environment. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the Thursday handoff, the artifact names, and the posting path for the next resilience update.

members.name: Lena Ortiz
members.expertise: Interagency coordination, emergency operations workflows, county planning briefings, WebEOC and mutual-aid coordination
members.background: Lena works in the county Emergency Management Office and coordinates information flow between public agencies, hospitals, NGOs, and the planning section during activations and preparedness cycles.
members.private_state: She wants the modeling output to be briefable this week without creating extra clarification work for the planning cell, and she is concerned that delayed or overly technical deliverables will make the simulation effort look disconnected from operations.
hidden_assumptions: A 'capacity snapshot' should reflect what agencies can actually staff and deploy at the start of the next operational period, including current shortages and partial outages.
The 'current baseline' already includes the newly added mutual-aid partners and NGO liaisons from last Friday's county roster update.
If something is 'ready for planning,' it is usable in a Thursday briefing even if the numbers may still be refined later, as long as the direction of change is trustworthy.
Posting an update to the 'common operating picture' means attaching a concise human-readable product inside the county's WebEOC workflow where planners already look for updates.

members.name: Ravi Menon
members.expertise: Network simulation, systems fragility modeling, resilience analytics, data pipeline management
members.background: Ravi leads a university-affiliated applied modeling team that builds agent- and network-based simulations of disaster response systems for public-sector partners.
members.private_state: He wants to preserve methodological consistency across runs and avoid introducing last-minute operational edits that break comparability, and he is concerned about being blamed for unstable outputs if a provisional run is treated as finalized.
hidden_assumptions: A 'capacity snapshot' refers to the standardized model input table derived from each organization's nominal resource profile under the scenario, not live staffing adjustments unless explicitly encoded.
The 'current baseline' is the last formally approved network package from the Q2 exercise, because only approved baselines should anchor comparative fragility runs.
A run is not 'ready' until the overnight reruns converge and the headline fragility values are stable within a narrow tolerance, even if a preliminary curve exists.
Updating the 'common operating picture' means refreshing the machine-readable service layer and metadata feed that downstream dashboards pull from, not manually posting a briefing attachment.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use the latest 'capacity snapshot' for Thursday's run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a near-real-time operational picture of deployable capacity at the start of the next operational period, including absenteeism, damaged facilities, and temporary shortages.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the standardized model input table representing nominal organizational capacity under the scenario configuration, unless a formal parameter update has been issued.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both regularly use the phrase 'capacity snapshot' and both regard their meaning as the obvious one for coordination, so the term sounds precise enough that neither thinks to unpack it.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to building Thursday's update off the 'current baseline.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the county roster and interagency map updated last Friday to include two voluntary organizations and a regional dialysis mutual-aid partner.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the previously approved Q2 baseline scenario package used in earlier comparison runs, which does not yet include those additions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each assumes there is one clearly recognized latest baseline, and because both have recently handled something labeled 'baseline,' the phrase gives a false sense of shared reference.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as ready for planning
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align that the fragility update should be 'ready for planning' by Thursday afternoon.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the output is ready once it can support a planning-cell conversation and indicate where coordination degrades, even if some values are preliminary.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the output is ready only after reruns complete and the fragility threshold and network-efficiency values have stabilized to his lab's internal reproducibility standard.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'ready' is usually treated as a practical scheduling term rather than a technical acceptance criterion, so both assume the other shares their threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: How the update gets posted to the common operating picture
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Ravi will 'push the update to the common operating picture' after the run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a one-page summary graphic and PDF attachment to appear in WebEOC under the planning board so planners can use it directly in the briefing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to refresh the ArcGIS/service-layer endpoint and deposit the supporting files in the shared analytics bucket, assuming the county dashboards will ingest it automatically.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are talking about the same downstream information environment and believe they are discussing distribution rather than method, so the implementation path stays implicit.
